paper_metadata.title: CCA3-SGAD: Quantum Amplitude Amplification for Combinatorial Search on Sparse Graphs — The First Explicit Crossover Condition for Heuristic-Biased Quantum Search over Classical Heuristic-Assisted Pipelines

summary: The paper’s main quantitative claims are a Grover-style crossover condition p > (C_oracle/M')^(2/3), with C_oracle ≈ 300 and a simulated crossover near M' ≈ 212,000 for p = 0.0126. It also reports a 3-qubit IBM ibm_fez hardware validation where biased amplitude amplification improved target probability from 0.693 to 0.872 on |101⟩ (Δ = +0.179, z = 27.7) with 8,192 shots per circuit.

experiments.description: Statevector simulation of biased Grover/amplitude amplification on a small Barabási–Albert graph with a planted 3-clique anomaly, comparing biased vs uniform initial states.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: peak success probability at the predicted Grover iteration count; simulation confirms O(1/sqrt(p)) scaling
algorithm.parameter_initialization: biased initial state prepared from heuristic scores; uniform condition uses uniform superposition

problem_formulation.encoding_details: candidate subgraphs indexed in computational basis; heuristic-biased initial amplitudes over candidate indices
problem_formulation.objective_function: find a connected induced k-node subgraph satisfying anomaly criteria A
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: phase oracle marks valid anomaly candidates; biased amplitude amplification used instead of uniform Grover

problem_instance.description: Synthetic small-scale graph anomaly detection instance with a planted hub-centred 3-clique anomaly
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: exact statevector simulation; compare peak success iteration and success probability for biased vs uniform Grover

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: heuristic scores computed for candidate subgraphs
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: measure success probability and compare to theory

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: success probability peaks at predicted iteration count

speedup_claims.conditions: biased amplitude amplification with heuristic prior p; scaling O(1/sqrt(p))
speedup_claims.caveats: Simulation-scale instance is small; paper also reports only marginal advantage at M' = 10^8.
Both methods find the planted anomaly; advantage is modest at this scale.

complexity_analysis.crossover_n: M' > (Coracle/M')^(2/3) as stated; simulation-scale crossover discussed at M'≈212,000

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established as a practical hardware crossover; simulation only on N=30, k=3, M=108.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 3-qubit statevector simulation; paper discusses a larger fault-tolerant roadmap of 364 logical qubits and 63,700 T-gates, but not for this experiment.
limiting_factors: no classical runtime comparison on the same instance

notes: The paper reports a NumPy statevector simulation but does not specify the qubit count for this small instance; num_qubits is therefore not directly reported. The experiment is clearly gate-based amplitude amplification, so it is included.
Paper reports O(1/sqrt(p)) scaling and a peak at the predicted iteration count, but this is a simulation result rather than a practical advantage demonstration.

The paper reports statistically significant biased-vs-uniform improvements on hardware, but only for a 3-qubit primitive, so this is not practical quantum advantage.
